text.p: Orbital Engine Co said on Thursday it was discussing further alliances in the automotive and motorcycle engine markets for its direct injection engine technology which should come to fruition over the coming year.

"The world-wide focus in direct injecting the conventional four stroke will see a number of new partners for Orbital and a significant growth in the engineering programmes in this sector," chief executive Kim Schlunke told the annual meeting.
"The growing Asian motorcycle market will be tapped by Orbital with engineering and pilot production programmes through next year," Schlunke said.

"Orbital will continue to brace itself for the rapid growth associated with successful commercialisation of a new technology by linking with major industry companies in alliances that leverage Orbital's technology and pilot manufacturing expertise and the experience, marketing and financial strength of our partners," Schlunke said.
He said Orbital had executed a vigourous cost-cutting programme through 1996 and this had build a slimmer, more efficient organisation.
He said new marine and personal water vehicle models would appear in 1997 and 1998.
"Pilot runs of automotive two strokes will appear in Indonesia and further brand names and models will appear," Schlunke said.
Orbital announced in September that its combustion process engine had been selected to power the planned Indonesian national car, the Maleo, which is scheduled to go into production in 1998.
The company reported a net loss of A$69.83 million for the year to June after a loss of A$7.79 million a year earlier.
Orbital shares closed two cents lower at A$1.00.
The stock has traded between 78 cents and A$1.25 this year.
